1→# DCTA improvement plan and implementation brief
   2→
   3→Consolidated **12 October 2026** from the original improvement plan and the implementation prompt. This is the single source for the next implementation work. Copy this document into an implementation chat, or ask an implementation agent to follow it. Architecture and information-flow diagrams: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).
   4→
   5→The original consolidation changed documentation only. Completed nickname features below are existing work; Phase 1 is now implemented with local verification recorded in STATUS.md; phases 2–6 remain proposed and must be verified before being marked complete.
   6→
   7→## Status and order
   8→
   9→| Work | Status | Next action |
  10→|---|---|---|
  11→| Seed aliases, spacing-insensitive matching, customer nicknames and near-spelling suggestions | Implemented in the working tree; preserve and regression-test | See completed work below |
  12→| Phase 1: readiness and development setup | Implemented; local verification in STATUS.md | Operator: configure matching tokens, restart and check `/api/ready`; live provider checks remain separate |
  13→| Phase 2: faster extraction | Proposed; small reasoning-control probe recorded | Evaluate full-workflow speed and accuracy before changing defaults |
  14→| Phase 3: fewer clarification rounds | Proposed | Collect related fields and support verified structured answers |
  15→| Phase 4: deadlines and reusable work | Proposed | Bound retries, reject stale results and avoid duplicate extraction |
  16→| Phase 5: truthful progress and recovery | Proposed | Report actual stages and recover safely after failures |
  17→| Phase 6: validation evidence and enrollment | Proposed | Supply bound calculation evidence and consume enrollment codes on success |
  18→
  19→The later review resolves three conflicts in the original plan: preserve the 34/35 accuracy baseline rather than allowing 33/35; report actual backend stages rather than guessing them with timers; and use the non-destructive database upgrade path rather than resetting existing passkeys and history. The original optional nickname proposal has already been implemented and is not a new task.
  20→
  21→## Completed work to preserve
  22→
  23→The original browser session exposed missing recognition of “mom” and “ahma”. Subsequent changes implemented:
  24→
  25→- **Bank aliases:** `payee-mum` includes Mom, Mummy, Mommy and Mama; `payee-ahma` includes Ahma, Ah Mah, Amah and Grandma. Do not add the ambiguous alias “Ma”. Aliases also feed voice hotwords.
  26→- **Shared exact matching:** [shared/names.py](../shared/names.py) is used by both [agent/names.py](../agent/names.py) and [gateway/evidence.py](../gateway/evidence.py). Matching ignores case, punctuation and spacing between words, but retains whole-word boundaries: “ahma”, “ah ma” and “Ah-Ma” can match Ah Ma; “mumbai” cannot match Mum. Preserve disambiguation of John versus John Doe.
  27→- **Near-spelling suggestions:** small edit distances, the same first letter, names of at least three letters and filler-word filtering produce choices such as “Ahmar” → Ah Ma or “Jhon” → John. These are suggestions only; fuzzy matches are never accepted directly as evidence. Show all relevant candidates and a none-of-these option.
  28→- **Customer nicknames:** the `payee_nicknames` table, Payees page (`#/payees`) and session/Origin-protected, audited gateway routes support nickname management. Conflicts with another payee, account, biller, card or stock are refused with `NICKNAME_CONFLICT`. The clarification card can offer to remember a nickname; the earlier receipt-only proposal is superseded. Nicknames feed bank reads, validator labels and ASR hotwords.
  29→- **Database upgrade:** `make upgrade-db` adds the table and new aliases without deleting enrolled passkeys or history. Do not use `make reset-db` on the user's existing database for this work.
  30→
  31→The earlier plan reported 48 nickname tests in [tests/test_payee_names.py](../tests/test_payee_names.py) and 46 passing attack scenarios. These are historical counts, not checks rerun by this consolidation. Verify that “mom” and “ahma” cases are also covered in the golden dataset; add them if missing, keep them separate from the original 35-case baseline, and disclose their development exposure rather than labelling them held-out without justification.
  32→
  33→## Implementation instructions
  34→
  35→Implement the following improvements to DCTA, prioritizing reliable completion and lower time from user input to an approvable draft. Preserve all existing payment features and security boundaries. Work through the phases in order, checking each phase before continuing. Inspect the current working tree first: it contains existing uncommitted work, including nickname support. Preserve it and do not reimplement completed features.
  36→
  37→Read `CODEBUDDY.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, the relevant folder READMEs and the recorded evaluations before editing. Treat historical reports as evidence from those runs, not proof that current code passes. Update the architecture's proposed/current labels only after the corresponding behavior is implemented and verified.
  38→
  39→## Evidence and objective
  40→
  41→- A read-only review on 12 October 2026 found seven locally recorded extraction calls from 11–12 October: median 13.6 seconds, range 7.3–24.2 seconds.
  42→- Both locally recorded validation attempts failed with `SERVICE_TOKEN_UNSET`. Settings loaded in the review process also reported the token unconfigured. Recheck configuration status without printing secrets; running services may have different environments.
  43→- The 10 October golden evaluation measured extractor median 8.943 seconds versus whole-agent median 8.972 seconds. Natural-draft validation added median 1.333 seconds. A recorded flow with two clarification answers took 39.1 seconds of processing across three requests.
  44→- The existing reasoning-control experiment used a small probe; its 1.5–1.6 second result is not a full-workflow benchmark or accuracy result.
  45→
  46→Primary targets: fail promptly on known configuration problems; reduce extractor median to at most 3 seconds and p95 to at most 6 seconds on the original golden set; reduce unnecessary clarification and retry model calls. These are targets to measure, not claims or guarantees. Measure complete input-to-ready time separately, including voice transcription when applicable; never sum independently computed percentiles as an end-to-end percentile.
  47→
  48→### Recorded reasoning-control probe (12 October)
  49→
  50→The original plan records these results for a small one-leg prompt using TokenHub `hy3`, temperature 0 and JSON mode. They are historical observations, not newly verified provider guarantees. Check the current official provider contract during implementation.
  51→
  52→| Request option (`extra_body`) | Time | Output tokens (reasoning) |
  53→|---|---|---|
  54→| none (current) | 5.9 s | 374 (356) |
  55→| `{"reasoning_effort": "high"}` | 5.1 s | 299 (281) |
  56→| `{"reasoning_effort": "low"}` | 3.7 s | 201 (183) |
  57→| **`{"reasoning_effort": "no_think"}`** | **1.5–1.6 s (3 runs)** | **17 (0)** |
  58→| **`{"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}`** | **1.7–1.8 s (2 runs)** | **17 (0)** |
  59→| `{"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "no_think"}}` | 4.6 s | 302 (284): ignored by TokenHub |
  60→| `{"enable_thinking": false}` | 6.0 s | 410 (392): ignored |
  61→
  62→The top-level `reasoning_effort` and `thinking` options reduced this probe's runtime; the nested `chat_template_kwargs` and `enable_thinking` options did not disable reasoning in that experiment. The 17-token response is much smaller than the full workflow's output, so the speedup cannot be assumed to transfer directly. Keep validator reasoning unchanged during the extractor comparison.
  63→
  64→## Non-negotiable constraints
  65→
  66→- Neither model may approve, sign, execute, write the ledger, or choose payment tools. Preserve service isolation and scoped gateway reads.
  67→- Keep the independent validator and fail closed on mismatch, uncertainty, invalid output, unavailable service or timeout. Do not relax validation to hit latency targets.
  68→- Preserve gateway evidence checks, exact record resolution, deterministic money calculations, immutable bundle/envelope binding, WebAuthn approval, hard policy checks, step-up, and atomic execution with audit and receipt. Keep the extractor and validator on different vendors.
  69→- Do not turn fuzzy name suggestions into accepted payment evidence. A user choice must be authenticated and bound to the correct question, field, payment leg and revision; gateway checks must validate it independently of the agent.
  70→- Corrections, expired quotes and relevant bank or mandate changes invalidate affected cached work and approval eligibility. Recheck live policy at execution. Repeated approval of the same operation must still return one receipt and cause at most one commit.
  71→- Do not edit `.env`, display secrets, reset the existing database, discard user changes, commit, push or deploy. Document required operator configuration with placeholders in `.env.example` and setup docs. Use isolated synthetic databases for tests and benchmarks. Record unavailable credentials or tools honestly and complete unaffected work.
  72→- Do not add a queue, cache server or additional agent framework unless the existing architecture cannot meet a demonstrated requirement. Explain any dependency added.
  73→
  74→## Phase 1 — Readiness before expensive work
  75→
  76→Inspect `shared/settings.py`, `gateway/app.py`, `gateway/orchestration.py`, `shared/clients/validator.py`, `validator/app.py`, `Makefile`, and frontend error handling.
  77→
  78→1. Separate liveness from readiness. Before starting extraction, detect missing/short validator credentials and unavailable required model/service configuration. Use bounded checks; avoid adding a model call or expensive network round trip to every request.
  79→2. Distinguish presence of credentials from authenticated connectivity: a health response saying a token exists does not prove the gateway and validator share the same token. Provide an authenticated, non-model readiness check or equivalent verified startup path for that distinction.
  80→3. Return stable, actionable errors and safe health details. Do not expose secret values, headers or user data. Show the user that the service is unavailable; give operator setup guidance in documentation/logs. Avoid offering repeated full drafting as the fix for a permanent configuration failure.
  81→4. Document the shared `VALIDATOR_SERVICE_TOKEN` requirement, matching values in both services, the minimum length, and restart requirements. Do not generate or write secrets into the checkout.
  82→5. Restore the original development-ergonomics work: report missing `VALIDATOR_SERVICE_TOKEN`, `OPERATOR_TOKEN` and `STEP_UP_SECRET` by name only, distinguishing drafting readiness from step-up availability. Make `make dev` clean up the processes it starts on exit and provide `make stop` scoped to this project's processes; avoid a broad `pkill` that could terminate unrelated services. Replace or remove the stale `make demo` placeholder. Retain the existing README guidance to use a supported passkey-capable browser at `http://localhost:5173`; do not duplicate guidance already present.
  83→
  84→Acceptance: missing/short or mismatched token cases fail before extraction; unavailable dependencies are bounded; healthy readiness permits normal work; secret values never appear in responses or logs. A configuration-error test must assert zero extractor calls. Development shutdown leaves no child service processes from that invocation and does not stop unrelated processes; missing step-up configuration is reported without unnecessarily disabling otherwise eligible low-risk drafting.
  85→
  86→## Phase 2 — Faster extraction, measured safely
  87→
  88→Inspect `agent/extraction.py`, `agent/app.py`, `shared/settings.py`, `prompts/extractor.md`, telemetry configuration and `infra/compose.yaml`.
  89→
  90→1. Add an explicit, validated extractor reasoning configuration such as `EXTRACT_REASONING_EFFORT`, including `.env.example`, Compose wiring and safe trace metadata. Preserve existing behavior when unset. Check the provider's current official contract before choosing request fields; do not send unsupported options to another provider.
  91→2. Evaluate disabled reasoning first, then low reasoning if necessary, using the full golden set and multi-turn clarification/correction scenarios. Do not change validator reasoning in the same experiment.
  92→3. Keep enough output budget for valid 1–4-leg JSON. The original proposal suggested testing 1024 output tokens with reasoning disabled; treat that as a candidate to measure, not an automatic new default. Lowering `max_tokens` alone is not the optimization. Reject truncation and malformed output.
  93→4. Reuse provider HTTP clients with explicit startup/shutdown lifecycle where appropriate, while keeping user tokens scoped per request. Treat connection reuse as a secondary improvement, not an explanation for the measured multi-second model delay.
  94→
  95→Acceptance: label runs by model, prompt hash, reasoning setting and token budget. Preserve historical baseline reports. Require zero unsafe drafts, at least the baseline 34/35 overall correct outcomes, and no regression on the existing clarification cases. Expand with nickname and follow-up cases and report those separately. If a candidate misses the quality gate, retain the safe default and report the result. If credentials are available, run paired baseline/candidate trials more than once and report sample sizes, p50/p95, errors, token use and available cost. Do not present fake-model timings as model performance.
  96→
  97→## Phase 3 — Clarification with fewer repeated model calls
  98→
  99→Inspect `agent/workflow.py`, `agent/questions.py`, conversation models/routes, evidence checking and `web/src/components/ClarifyCard.tsx`.
 100→
 101→1. Collect related missing fields into one understandable clarification group, instead of stopping at the first issue and discovering the next only after another model run. Preserve clear links to individual payment legs.
 102→2. Provide explicit payee/account choices where the gateway knows the candidates. Store authenticated selections with provenance in the conversation. Derive any quoted evidence from gateway-owned labels and the user's confirmed choice; never let an agent forge a user answer.
 103→3. For an unambiguous structured answer, update the affected fields deterministically without re-extracting unchanged text. Recompute dependent amounts and revalidate the resulting frozen bundle. Free text, changed intent, ambiguity and corrections must safely fall back to extraction.
 104→4. Preserve support for answers that change more than the requested field. Never silently retain an earlier amount, source or recipient after the user corrects it.
 105→
 106→Acceptance: a scenario missing both recipient and source can collect both together; a supported structured answer makes no extra extractor call; final validation still runs. Reject forged IDs, another user's records, stale question/revision references, wrong-leg answers and ambiguous choices. Re-run correction, nickname, relative-amount and attack cases.
 107→
 108→## Phase 4 — One deadline and reusable work
 109→
 110→Inspect orchestration, extractor retries, validator timeouts and the browser request helper. The existing 45-second gateway wait is shorter than the extractor's 60-second request timeout with one SDK retry.
 111→
 112→1. Propagate an end-to-end deadline across gateway, agent and provider calls; give each stage only the remaining budget. Bound retries and admission/queue waiting within it. Handle cancellation honestly: closing an HTTP request does not guarantee a remote model stops generating.
 113→2. After cancellation, timeout or superseding input, prevent late results from being published or starting new downstream work. Preserve mandatory audit of state changes.
 114→3. Deduplicate simultaneous drafting for the same owner and revision. Design for the supported process/deployment model; document any single-process limitation rather than assuming an in-memory lock works across workers.
 115→4. Reuse an existing frozen draft for a validation-only retry if its conversation, payload, bank metadata, quote validity and other required bindings are still current. Reuse an eligible stored MATCH only under existing eligibility checks. Changed inputs must trigger the required rebuild/revalidation.
 116→5. Keep validation attempt/rate limits and exactly-once settlement behavior. Do not retry permanent configuration or semantic errors as transient failures.
 117→
 118→Acceptance: simulated slow providers return within the configured overall budget plus documented scheduling tolerance; no new stage starts after expiry; stale results cannot reach confirmation. Concurrent same-revision requests do not duplicate extraction. A retry after a transient validation failure reuses valid drafting work, while an edit or expired quote prevents reuse.
 119→
 120→## Phase 5 — Truthful progress and recovery
 121→
 122→Inspect `web/src/components/Chat.tsx`, `web/src/api.ts`, voice capture and backend orchestration. Choose bounded authenticated polling or server events based on the simplest maintainable implementation.
 123→
 124→1. Report actual stage transitions: captured/transcribing, extracting, resolving, validating, ready, needs input or failed. Show elapsed time and accessible announcements using the existing `useAnnounce` mechanism. Never use a timer to claim a stage the backend has not reached.
 125→2. Scope progress to an owned operation/revision, and prevent late responses from replacing a newer conversation. Stop polling/subscriptions on completion, cancellation and unmount.
 126→3. Provide bounded browser requests and recovery after timeout or reload. If an approval request has an unknown result, retrieve the existing authorization/receipt before suggesting another payment.
 127→4. Make validation-only retry distinct from rebuilding a corrected draft. Explain permanent configuration failures without a misleading retry loop.
 128→5. For voice, make transcript correction understandable. If allowing edits while drafting, supersede in-flight work safely. Do not add a mandatory extra confirmation click without a clear usability reason.
 129→
 130→Acceptance: progress matches real backend state; delayed responses, reloads, navigation and corrections cannot show stale confirmation. Screen-reader updates are useful without announcing every elapsed second. Aborting a draft does not claim to cancel an already approved/committed payment.
 131→
 132→## Phase 6 — Validation evidence and enrollment reliability
 133→
 134→1. Extend gateway-built validation input with the minimum calculation evidence needed for derived amounts such as “the rest”: source balance snapshot, ordered preceding debits, relevant dependencies and resulting amount. Use exact money types. Bind this evidence into request hashes and eligibility/invalidation logic; do not rely on extractor reasoning or unfrozen live values. Preserve privacy rules and execution-time checks.
 135→2. Distinguish semantic agreement from deterministic risk policy. Investigate the five historical false rejects, including injected/coercive wording, without suppressing real uncertainty or weakening scam controls. Evaluate deliberately wrong drafts as well as correct ones; report mismatches, uncertainties and errors separately.
 136→3. In enrollment, validate/reserve the enrollment code when beginning, but consume it only in the successful credential-registration transaction. Preserve the existing 15-minute code expiry and single successful use, bind challenges to the code, bound repeated begins (the original proposal suggested five), and invalidate sibling challenges after success.
 137→
 138→Acceptance: correct remaining-balance drafts can be verified from supplied evidence; altered balances/dependencies or amounts cannot reuse validation improperly. No previously blocked wrong-draft probe becomes accepted. Enrollment begin → cancel → begin → verify succeeds; expired codes, concurrent successful uses, old sibling challenges and replay remain blocked.
 139→
 140→## Verification and delivery
 141→
 142→- Add meaningful regression tests for the behavior above, including failed readiness without model work, timeout propagation, deduplication, stale-result handling, validation-only retry, structured-answer provenance, derived-amount binding and enrollment races.
 143→- Run relevant tests during each phase, then the full backend suite, lint, frontend type check/build and fake evaluation harness. Re-run the rogue-agent/attack checks and affected isolation checks. Avoid resetting the user's database or automatically reinstalling dependencies unnecessarily.
 144→- Add browser tests for clarification, voice correction, progress, retry, reload and approval recovery. Use isolated fixtures/software authenticators for automation; separately document any real Touch ID/microphone walkthrough actually performed.
 145→- Run live model evaluations and sanitized Langfuse read-back when configured. If blocked, retain safe defaults and report exactly which acceptance gates remain unverified. Never fabricate performance, security, browser or live-backend results.
 146→- Update folder READMEs, setup guidance, [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), [JUDGE_QA.md](JUDGE_QA.md), the main README examples and evidence with actual results. Record the reasoning comparison in a new dated evidence report, such as `docs/evidence/T-14-no-think.md`, without overwriting the baseline. Preserve historical measurements. Report extractor, validator, ASR and complete request timings separately, plus model-call counts per completed task and clarification count.
 147→- Finish with what changed, measured before/after results, checks that passed, remaining limitations and required operator configuration. Do not claim completion of a phase whose acceptance gates remain unmet.
 148→

Values below are the defaults reviewed on 12 October, not an assertion about running services. `EXTRACT_REASONING_EFFORT` is proposed and is not wired into the current extractor. Phase 1 adds non-model authenticated readiness and configurable extractor timeout/retries; full deadline propagation remains proposed.

Operators must restart the relevant services after changing their environment and verify Compose passes each service only the credentials it needs.  171→
 172→## Verification commands
 173→
 174→Use the existing project commands where appropriate: `make test`, `make lint`, `make eval-fake`, `make eval` for configured live providers, and the frontend's `npm run build` after dependencies are installed. `make web-build` currently also runs `npm install`; avoid unnecessary reinstalls. Run `scripts/rogue_agent_demo.py` with isolated synthetic data and affected isolation checks as required. Browser tests added by the implementation need a documented command. These are implementation instructions, not commands executed by the documentation merge.

1→# CODEBUDDY.md — DCTA project rules
   2→
   3→Project: DBS track, Scenario 1, Direct Conversational Transaction Agent. Read `docs/PLAN.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/instructions.md`. v0.3 retains the full MVP at the user's request. **Langfuse is a required real observability backend**, not an optional exporter or console-log substitute. All implementation tasks remain pending until their checks actually pass.
   4→
   5→**Scope and authority**
   6→
   7→Keep SGD transfers (own account/saved payee/saved PayNow), bill payments, card payments, mock SGX equities, 1–4-leg bundles, dependencies, voice/text, clarification/corrections, WebAuthn, mandates/cooling/pause, KYC/risk/scam controls, simulated secondary approval, audit/evidence UI and evaluations. Tencent APM, TTS and public hosting are optional. `docs/PLAN_REVIEW.md` contains recommendations, including scope cuts the user has not adopted. Do not implement those cuts or silently replace real WebAuthn with a mock. Report schedule/integration blockers honestly.
   8→
   9→GenAI generates drafts and fallible semantic assessments; it never authorizes funds. Model calls exist only in agent extraction and the separate read-only validator. The workflow is fixed by code; models do not select tools. Treat either or both models returning a malicious MATCH as an expected test condition. Never describe a prompt as injection-proof or a model result as a signature.
  10→
  11→**Invariants — enforce with meaningful checks**
  12→
  13→- I1: agent and validator have no ledger mount/write access, execution dispatcher or signing credentials. Forbid imports of gateway/ledger in both; check transitive shared-code boundaries and actual runtime permissions.
  14→- I2: execution requires valid user approval bound to the exact gateway-stored signing envelope, operation and authenticated owner. Verify source ownership and credential/session binding, not just signature validity.
  15→- I3: confirmation renders that same gateway envelope. Edits create a new revision and supersede validation and approval.
  16→- I4: approvals and secondary proofs are fresh/single-use. Concurrent/repeated requests cause at most one commit; committed retries return the stored receipt.
  17→- I5: hard mandate, KYC, sanctions, ownership, funds and velocity blocks cannot be overridden by model output or secondary approval. Keep old mandate active during cooling; decreases/pauses cancel pending increases.
  18→- I6: required audit events commit with financial effects. Workflow stages have correlated Langfuse observations; live backend traces/experiments are required acceptance evidence.
  19→- I7: trusted code assigns source lineage and preserves derived dependencies/taint. Untrusted references cannot become critical fields via relabeling; valid span references do not prove semantic correctness.
  20→- I8: semantic uncertainty, errors and malformed output prevent approval. The agent cannot supply its own verdict. Even a validator forced to MATCH cannot bypass I1–I5.
  21→- I9: ordered mock bundles are all-or-nothing. Approved equity quantities, price constraints and debit remain fixed; expiry/changes require a new draft and approval.
  22→
  23→**Contracts**
  24→
  25→Use `SHA256(b"DCTA:approval:v1\x00" + canonical_bytes(SigningEnvelope))` in one shared helper for both challenge issuance and verification. Envelope contains schema version, operation, user/credential, operation ID, frozen full payload, conversation binding where applicable, active mandate version, nonce and timestamps. Gateway stores the bytes; execute accepts authorization ID, expected hash and assertion, never a replacement payment payload. Use distinct execute_bundle/update_mandate operations. TTL <=120 seconds and no later than quote expiry.
  26→
  27→Gateway captures original authenticated conversation turns and corrections; agent credentials cannot fabricate user turns. Gateway invokes validator directly with full ordered history, frozen bundle and bank mappings. Exclude extractor reasoning. Validator prompt/model/schema are backend-controlled, versioned and recorded; never accept system instructions from client fields or expose secrets in prompts. Bind results to bundle/conversation hashes and revisions. No live runtime bypass flags for tests.
  28→
  29→Execution and secondary approval use the state machine in ARCHITECTURE. Atomically recheck policy/state and commit effects, nonce/proof consumption, counters, receipt and audit. Recheck immediately after step-up as well. Idempotency uses user+operation+operation ID with immutable payload hash. Validation is required for conversational bundles; direct signed mandate settings use deterministic validation. Invalid signatures never become approvals.
  30→
  31→**Stack, files and permissions**
  32→
  33→Python 3.12/uv; FastAPI, Pydantic/settings, LangGraph, provider-compatible client, webauthn, Langfuse, httpx, cryptography; pytest/ruff. SQLite belongs to gateway. React/Vite/TypeScript/Tailwind and SimpleWebAuthn browser helper. Pin tested SDK versions; the prior Langfuse v3 assumption is superseded by current official docs. Check account-level model/ASR/backend access instead of assuming trial credits.
  34→
  35→```
  36→agent/        fixed workflow, extraction and READ/DRAFT API clients
  37→validator/    internal semantic audit service without payment tools
  38→gateway/      identity, captured conversation, frozen drafts, validation coordinator,
  39→              policy/mandates, approval/step-up, execution and audit
  40→ledger/       gateway-only mock bank models and seed
  41→shared/       pure types/canonicalization, safe telemetry and scoped HTTP clients
  42→prompts/      version-controlled instructions
  43→web/          chat/audio, confirmation, mandate settings, evidence viewer
  44→infra/        isolated service images/Compose
  45→evals/        versioned datasets, Langfuse experiment runner and reports
  46→tests/        contracts, model fixtures, gateway, isolation, lifecycle and attacks
  47→```
  48→
  49→Only gateway has the ledger/evidence mount and identity/secondary-approval secrets. Agent/validator receive narrowly scoped service credentials and their own model keys. Internal routes check service scope and owner/session binding. Shared utilities must not smuggle execution capabilities across the boundary. Never mount a Docker socket or full host workspace into the agent runtime.
  50→
  51→**Langfuse and audit handling**
  52→
  53→Use a configured Langfuse project with real generation/workflow traces and evaluation experiments. No-op exporters are test fixtures only. Share trace context across services, link resumed turns through pseudonymous session/revision IDs, and persist trace IDs in audit. Log prompt version/hash, model, safe input/output, latency and available usage/cost; missing cost is unavailable, not zero. Do not leave spans open during human waiting.
  54→
  55→Allowlist/redact before export, including errors. Never send API keys, auth headers/cookies, OTPs, assertions, private keys, raw audio or full account IDs to Langfuse. Disable indiscriminate argument capture. Keep raw evidence access-controlled locally and use synthetic model-visible banking data. Langfuse outage must show degraded health and bounded export retry without changing authorization or re-executing payments. Local mandatory audit failure blocks commit. Do not claim the local hash chain is regulatory-grade or protected against a privileged complete rewrite.
  56→
  57→**Implementation discipline**
  58→
  59→- Decimal for money; serialize two-decimal strings. SQLite integer minor units or validated decimal strings, never REAL. Reject float/non-finite values and unsupported precision.
  60→- UTC timestamps in storage/signing; Asia/Singapore calendar days for daily policy.
  61→- Pydantic schemas at HTTP/model boundaries; type hints; small readable functions. No arbitrary expression evaluation, model HTML or model-selected tools.
  62→- Schema-valid model output can still be false. Semantic checks and deterministic authorization are tested/reported separately.
  63→- Tests cover meaningful financial, authorization, lifecycle and privacy behavior. Documentation-only changes use consistency/link checks; do not invent a test run when no app exists.

  24→**Security principle and threat model**
  25→
  26→GenAI produces drafts and semantic assessments. It cannot authorize funds. Assume either model can hallucinate, obey injected instructions or return `MATCH` for a bad draft. Both models have no execution tools, ledger access, signing keys or ability to change policy. Different vendors may provide useful diversity; reduced correlated error is a hypothesis to measure.
  27→
  28→Trusted components are the authenticated input capture, application confirmation UI, gateway code and identity store, ledger permissions, and validator-service configuration. Attacker-controlled content includes speech/text, references, labels and model output. A compromised browser, authenticator, gateway host or deployment credential is outside this prototype's demonstrated guarantees. A user may also approve a mistaken or socially engineered payment; cryptographic binding does not prove informed intent.
  29→
  30→The semantic validator is not immune to prompt injection. Deterministic checks do not interpret free text as instructions, but still require correct implementation.   32→**Workflow and service ownership**
  33→
  34→1. The authenticated client submits text, final ASR transcripts and corrections to a gateway-owned conversation store. Original audio is retained separately with a digest. Distinguish user turns, ASR revisions, bank data and application questions; preserve all versions. The drafting agent cannot append fabricated user turns.
  35→2. The agent reads a scoped snapshot, bounds input size, extracts structured slots, parses supported amounts and obtains account/payee/biller/card/quote metadata over read APIs. No model chooses tools.
  36→3. Deterministic resolution returns all plausible candidates. Missing or ambiguous values trigger short questions. Corrections create a new conversation revision; never silently change an approved draft.
  37→4. The agent proposes a bundle. The gateway validates the schema, ownership and metadata, computes dependency arithmetic, canonicalizes the resolved bundle and freezes its version. Agent-supplied names, provenance labels and totals are not authoritative.
  38→5. The gateway requests validation from a separate read-only validator service using its stored conversation, exact frozen bundle and minimum bank metadata. It obtains the result directly, checks the output schema and binds the result to the bundle and conversation hashes. Agent-supplied “validation passed” flags are rejected.
  39→6. A successful semantic check and deterministic pre-check allow the gateway to issue a signing envelope. The client fetches it directly from the gateway and renders precise details, totals, residual cash and any changes.
  40→7. WebAuthn approval is bound to the full envelope. After verification the gateway rechecks live policy; any required secondary approval is bound to the same transaction. Only then may one atomic mock-ledger commit execute the legs and return a receipt.
  41→8. Every stage produces audit events and correlated Langfuse observations. A receipt supports “You said → We clarified → You approved → Executed.” Technical hashes are expandable details.

  43→The agent uses READ and DRAFT functions only.   45→**Validator contract and prompt protection**
  46→
  47→The validator's job is to compare all requested actions against all drafted actions, including beneficiary, amount, currency, source account, asset, quantity and dependencies. Its inputs contain the complete ordered conversation including clarification questions and user corrections, an immutable bundle, and authoritative ID-to-display mappings. It receives no extractor reasoning or extractor-written summary. Bank labels are evidence, not instructions. An incorrect ASR transcript may fool both models, so the user must see and be able to correct it.
  48→
  49→Use a fixed, version-controlled system prompt on the validator backend. Users and the agent cannot set its instructions, model or output schema. Keep secrets out of prompts and design as if the prompt is public. Separate policy instructions from serialized data, bound input sizes, and require structured output; these are mitigations, not proof against injection. Do not truncate relevant history silently: require a fresh explicit restatement when the supported context budget is exceeded. Prompt changes require review and evaluation, and prompt version/hash is logged to Langfuse. Avoid mutable remote prompt labels during a demonstration.
  50→
  51→Return `MATCH | MISMATCH | UNCERTAIN` and bounded issues containing leg ID, field, short reason, supported value when known, and evidence turn/span references. No tool calls, transaction edits, repair execution or arbitrary HTML. Server code verifies field names and evidence locations; a valid reference does not prove the model's interpretation is correct.
  52→
  53→- MATCH: eligible for confirmation only, never authorization.
  54→- MISMATCH: freeze this draft and show deterministic field-level feedback; any correction creates a new version and revalidation.
  55→- UNCERTAIN: ask for clarification; do not approve.
  56→- Timeout, unavailable model, malformed JSON or unknown verdict: stop approval with a retry option; no fallback to MATCH.
  57→

  60→**Signing and execution contract**
  61→
  62→Money uses Decimal and serializes as two-decimal strings; reject floats, non-finite/negative values and excessive precision. Mock equity prices are also two-decimal SGD values. All signed timestamps have one UTC ISO-8601 Z format. Canonical JSON has sorted object keys, compact separators and UTF-8; array order is meaningful. IDs and strings are validated before freezing; do not normalize them after signing.
  63→
  64→The versioned `SigningEnvelope` contains `schema_version`, `operation` (`execute_bundle` or `update_mandate`), authenticated `user_id`, `credential_id`, `bundle_id` or `change_id`, full immutable payload, conversation binding for a bundle, active mandate version, a random 32-byte nonce, `issued_at` and `expires_at`. Expires at most 120 seconds after issue, and no later than a quote's expiry. Do not allow client-selected users or operation changes.
  65→
  66→`challenge = SHA256(b"DCTA:approval:v1\x00" + canonical_bytes(envelope))`.
  67→
  68→Use this exact function when issuing and verifying. Store the envelope bytes and hash server-side. Execute requests carry the authorization ID, expected envelope hash and assertion, not a replacement payment payload. The gateway executes its stored payload. Verify session, credential ownership, origin, RP ID, user verification, expected challenge, validity and current revision; require a new challenge after any edit. Signed mandate operations cannot authorize payments.
  69→
  70→WebAuthn RP ID and origin are bound to the host: `localhost` works over plain HTTP on the development laptop (Touch ID via Chrome/Safari), but a phone requires an HTTPS origin, and credentials enrolled on one RP ID do not work on another. Record the demo on the laptop unless a hosted HTTPS deployment is tested and re-enrolled. WebAuthn user verification may use a PIN or biometrics. A React overlay remains trusted application UI, not a browser-protected payment confirmation surface. Do not equate this implementation with Secure Payment Confirmation. Source accounts, owned cards and payees must belong to or be operable by the authenticated user, regardless of signature validity.
  71→
  72→Authorization states: `PENDING_APPROVAL → AWAITING_STEP_UP → COMMITTED`, or directly `PENDING_APPROVAL → COMMITTED`; terminal alternatives are `BLOCKED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`, `SUPERSEDED`. A step-up transition retains verified approval evidence but does not move funds. Only one terminal commit is allowed. Store the secondary challenge against the user, envelope hash, approval ID and expiry; verify through a separate simulated channel, with single-use proof and bounded attempts. The agent cannot create or complete that proof.
  73→
  74→Dispatch deterministic policy by operation type. Signed mandate settings require authenticated ownership and valid change rules, not a semantic MATCH or sufficient funds for a payment. A paused/expired spending mandate must not prevent its owner from submitting an authorized settings change; relaxation still observes cooling. Payment-only eligibility checks cannot be bypassed by changing the signed operation type.
  75→
  76→Commit policy rechecks, balance/holding mutations, daily/velocity counters, nonce consumption, secondary-proof consumption, receipt and mandatory audit event in one SQLite transaction. Recheck state under the transaction lock to handle concurrent requests. Idempotency is scoped to `(user_id, operation, bundle_id/change_id)` and the immutable payload hash: the identical authenticated retry returns the original receipt; changed payload with that key rejects. Retry after a lost response must not repeat effects. In-flight step-up retries return the same pending status, never consume the proof twice.

It holds no keys or tokens: the session is an HttpOnly cookie and passkey private keys stay in the authenticator. The UI cannot approve anything by itself. It signs the WebAuthn options the gateway derived from the stored envelope. The gateway then re-verifies the signature, the owner, the envelope hash and all policy before committing. Model-written text (validator reasons, clarification questions, transcripts) is rendered as plain text through React escaping. There is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.   63→## Accessibility
  64→
  65→Labelled controls and fieldsets, a skip link, and visible 3 px focus outlines. Focus moves to the page heading on navigation, to the confirmation/clarification/receipt heading when it appears, and to error messages. Status updates go to one polite `aria-live` region; the countdown is `role=timer` (not chatty), with one 30-second warning. Nothing is conveyed by colour alone: badges and notices carry words and symbols, changes show "before → after" text with strikethrough, and the current page is marked with `aria-current` and underline. Amounts are 30 px and tabular. Touch targets are at least 44 px. Layout is single-column and works at 375 px. Reduced motion is respected.
